Replay

Durable checkpoint assets

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Dependency policyPackage and persistenceRoom integration

Use a checkpoint package when restoring gameplay requires external assets as well as state. A room publication can include its complete external asset set in the same transaction as its checkpoint. The authority Point continues to name the raw typed checkpoint. A separate signed payload descriptor names the transferred package; the package verifies its root against that Point and checks every asset's content hash. Restore grants still select the exact checkpoint publication.

Dependency policy#

The deployment and game supply the same Asset_Policy:

Odin
policy := checkpoint.Asset_Policy{
    collect = game.checkpoint_assets,
    validate = scenegd.asset_png_valid,
}
backend.assets = policy
room_options.checkpoint_assets = policy
room_options.checkpoint_cache = &asset_cache

collect receives the raw checkpoint, a bounded reference buffer and an optional borrowed checkpoint codec. It must enumerate all required assets, including executable pending work. Return false on overflow or invalid input. Zero references and duplicates are normalized; malformed references fail. The callback may decode the checkpoint with its deployment-selected model but must not mutate it or call back into storage. validate checks actual asset content and is mandatory for a nonempty dependency set.

Room builds reusable schema metadata before acquiring authority and shares it with checkpoint encoding, decoding and dependency collection. Collectors may use that codec for their declared model while it remains borrowed; they must not destroy or retain it. Packaging enumerates dependencies once and validates the encoded entries without decoding the root again solely to repeat the same enumeration.

Scrapyard's collector includes current player sprays and accepted executable pending Set_Spray declarations. Its service and Room validate PNG data through the existing bounded Godot image decoder. Rejected/retired declarations do not require an asset that will never be installed.

The service requires an exact asset set: missing, extra, corrupt and semantically invalid entries are refused before publication. A game without declared external dependencies continues to use raw checkpoints. Undeclared extra uploads are not accepted as a general-purpose storage bucket.

Package and persistence#

The transfer package is a canonical envelope around the existing asset bundle. The full payload, including checkpoint and assets, is limited to 1 MiB and 32 unique references, matching the room transfer profile. Each asset remains subject to its game/cache limits. The local-file bundle profile retains its separate 16 MiB limit. bundle_encode accepts a lower caller-selected bound and checks it before allocating the output; room packaging uses that preflight.

The SQLite store adds replay_room_checkpoint_package. Raw checkpoint, publication metadata and package are written/removed atomically. A single joined read obtains one coherent publication/package snapshot. Package framing, root identity, asset hashes and model dependency policy are checked before a typed load returns data. A zero-length or corrupt package row is not treated as an absent package.

Restore's commit guard compares the package descriptor as well as the publication, so the package cannot disappear or change between validation and the authority decision. Existing raw checkpoint publications remain readable for models that require no assets. A legacy raw checkpoint that requires missing assets fails validation; it is not silently acknowledged as complete or repaired with guessed data. Back up the complete private database, including this table.

Saved.bytes owns the raw checkpoint and Saved.payload owns the optional package. Destroy them together with saved_destroy. The stored package duplicates its root, so on-disk root-plus-package data is bounded by twice the 1 MiB root limit per room; transfer bytes remain at most 1 MiB. Repeated publications replace the previous package; there is no unbounded asset history or cross-room asset sharing.

Room integration#

Room packages assets from the borrowed cache after capturing its immutable root. Missing cache data prevents upload. The transfer owns its accepted bytes, so later cache changes cannot alter that in-flight package. A lost reply is resolved through the current validated publication, as with raw checkpoints.

During recovery, Room validates dependency completeness and installs the package into its cache before the existing preparation callback and restore request. bundle_install preflights the complete set and cache capacity before mutation. The cache must outlive Room; the game still owns texture/material construction. Installing bytes does not grant authority.

Checkpoint-transfer protocol 3 adds the payload descriptors and v3 HMAC domain. Clients and services must upgrade together. Publication metadata, authority Record, private Bundle, gameplay protocol and raw checkpoint formats remain unchanged.

Bundled transfer deliberately starts with one complete durable snapshot. It does not implement cross-publication deduplication, independent asset uploads or saves beyond this transfer bound. Save age, transfer duration and the room's existing rollback policy remain separate: a durable checkpoint can still be too old for a restore grant. No recovery-policy limit is relaxed by asset publication.
